# Vivla Skill Reference

## Product summary

Vivla is a co-ownership real estate platform with a mobile app for property owners, an internal tools suite for operations, a REST API for bookings and properties, and a CX panel for customer support. The ecosystem spans 11 repositories organized into four domains: core products (vivla-api, vivla-mobile-app, vivla-tools, vivla-panel), services (booking-cloud-functions, calendar-manager, VivlaNPS), deep links (vivla-app-site, app-invites), and external development (propcos).

The platform runs on two independent backends: **Vivla API** (NestJS 11, PostgreSQL via TypeORM, serves mobile app and CX panel) and **Tools API** (NestJS 10, Supabase PostgreSQL, serves mobile chat/surveys and internal tools). All frontends route through Cloudflare for DNS, CDN, and access control.

**Key files and commands:**
- `.env.development` — environment variables (never commit real values)
- `src/main.ts` — API entry point with versioning config
- `npm run build:development` / `npm run build:preview` / `npm run build:production` — mobile builds
- `npm install` — installs Husky git hooks automatically
- Swagger UI at `/api/docs` (development only)

**Primary docs:** https://wiki.vivla.com

---

## When to use

Reach for this skill when:

- **Building mobile features** — adding screens, modules, or integrations to the React Native app (vivla-mobile-app)
- **Extending the API** — adding endpoints, validations, or business logic to vivla-api or Tools API
- **Working with bookings** — understanding reservation workflows, calendar slots, keys (exchange currency), or rental logic
- **Configuring environments** — setting up `.env` files, database connections, or external service integrations
- **Debugging integrations** — troubleshooting chat (Stream Chat), notifications (push/email), or third-party syncs (HubSpot, Notion, Slack)
- **Understanding architecture** — mapping how the mobile app, panel, and internal tools connect to backends
- **Deploying or releasing** — managing builds, deployments to Railway, or app store submissions
- **Working with the CX panel** — building or fixing features in vivla-panel for customer support agents

---

## Quick reference

### Repository structure

| Repo | Purpose | Stack | Hosting |
|------|---------|-------|---------|
| `vivla-api` | Main API (bookings, auth, properties) | NestJS 11, PostgreSQL, Firestore | Railway |
| `vivla-tools` | Internal platform (chat, surveys, notifications) | NestJS 10, Supabase, TanStack Start | Railway |
| `vivla-mobile-app` | iOS/Android app | React Native 0.81, Expo SDK 54 | App Store / Play |
| `vivla-panel` | CX backoffice | TBD | TBD |
| `booking-cloud-functions` | Automations & integrations | Firebase Functions, Node.js 20 | Google Firebase |

### API versioning

- **v1 endpoints** — `/v1/...` (new routes, follow conventions: envelope `object`, cursor pagination, structured errors)
- **v2 endpoints** — `/v2/...` (keys, experiences, newer features)
- **Legacy routes** — `/api/...` (maintain historical shape for backward compatibility)
- **Public routes** — `/api/public/...` (no auth, API key guard)

### Environment variables (never commit real values)

**Mobile app** (`.env.development`):
- `API_URL` — Vivla API base URL
- `CHAT_API_URL` — Tools API chat endpoint
- `STREAM_API_KEY` — Stream Chat API key
- `SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` — error tracking
- `POSTHOG_API_KEY`, `POSTHOG_HOST` — analytics
- `EAS_PROJECT_ID`, `EAS_UPDATE_URL` — Expo build config

**Panel** (`.env.template`):
- `VITE_APP_ENV` — `development`, `staging`, or `production`
- `VITE_API_BASE_URL` — Vivla API URL
- `VITE_AUTH0_DOMAIN`, `VITE_AUTH0_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_AUTH0_AUDIENCE` — Auth0 config
- `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` — error tracking
- `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` — for source map uploads (staging/prod only)

### Common API patterns

**Request ID** — Every response includes `X-Request-ID` header. If client sends one, server respects it. Useful for support tickets.

**Idempotency** — Send `Idempotency-Key: <string>` header on mutations to make them safe for retries. Same key = same response without re-executing logic.

**Rate limits** — Default 100 req/min per IP. Response headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`. On 429, respect `Retry-After`.

**Error envelope** — All errors follow:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "validation_error",
    "message": "...",
    "request_id": "req_...",
    "details": [{ "path": "field", "message": "..." }]
  }
}
```

**Pagination** — Cursor-based with `has_more` and `next_cursor`:
```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [...],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "eyJ..."
}
```

---

## Decision guidance

### When to use v1 vs v2 endpoints

| Scenario | Use |
|----------|-----|
| Booking CRUD, calendar, availability | v1 (`/v1/bookings/...`) |
| Keys wallet, movements, experiences | v2 (`/v2/bookings/keys/...`, `/v2/bookings/experiences/...`) |
| Admin operations (create, edit, cancel) | v1 admin (`/v1/admin/bookings/...`) |
| Key transfers, metrics, charts | v2 admin (`/v2/admin/bookings/keys/...`) |

### When to use Vivla API vs Tools API

| Feature | API | Reason |
|---------|-----|--------|
| Bookings, reservations, properties | Vivla API | Core business logic, Firestore source of truth |
| Chat, surveys, notifications | Tools API | Real-time messaging, mobile-specific endpoints |
| User auth, profile | Vivla API | Primary auth system (JWT) |
| Admin users, teams, permissions | Tools API | Internal operations, Auth0 integration |

### When to deploy: OTA update vs full build

| Change | Deploy type | Time |
|--------|-------------|------|
| JS/TS code only | OTA update (Expo) | ~5 min |
| Native code, config, dependencies | Full build | ~30 min (dev), ~60 min (prod) |
| Commit message contains `[build]` | Force full build | — |

---

## Workflow

### Adding a new API endpoint

1. **Identify the version and module** — Is this v1 (bookings, calendar) or v2 (keys, experiences)? Which module owns it?
2. **Check existing patterns** — Read a similar endpoint in the same controller to match conventions (envelope, error handling, auth guard).
3. **Write the controller method** — Add `@Get()`, `@Post()`, etc. with `@RequirePermission()` if admin-only.
4. **Add validation** — Use Zod schema or class-validator. Validate in the service, not the controller.
5. **Handle errors** — Throw `BadRequestException`, `ForbiddenException`, or custom errors. The global error filter converts them to the standard envelope.
6. **Test locally** — Hit the endpoint with curl or Postman. Check the response shape matches conventions.
7. **Document** — Add a comment with `@reference` linking to Notion (if applicable) or add a page to the wiki.

### Configuring a new environment variable

1. **Add to `.env.example`** — Document the variable with a comment explaining its purpose.
2. **Add to `.env.development`** — Copy `.env.example` to `.env.development` and fill in local values.
3. **Load in config** — In `src/config/env.ts` (panel) or `src/config/configuration.ts` (backend), read the variable with `process.env.VARIABLE_NAME`.
4. **Validate at startup** — Throw an error if required variables are missing.
5. **Never commit real values** — Use `.env.example` as the template; `.env.development` and `.env.production` are gitignored.

### Debugging a booking workflow issue

1. **Identify the booking ID** — Find it in the panel or mobile app.
2. **Check the booking state** — Call `GET /v1/admin/bookings/:id` to see status, type (enjoy/rent/exchange), and dates.
3. **Review the rules** — Read [Reglas de reserva](/backend/reglas-de-reserva) to understand what validations apply.
4. **Check the calendar** — Call `GET /v1/bookings/home-calendar/:homeId` to see slot availability and season.
5. **Trace the error** — If an operation failed, check the API response `error.code` and `details`. Look up the code in [Códigos de error](/tools/api/errors).
6. **Check the database** — For v1 (Firestore), inspect the booking document in Firebase Console. For v2 (Postgres), query the `exchange_keys_wallet` or `exchange_keys` tables.

### Deploying the mobile app

1. **Ensure tests pass** — `npm run test` locally and in CI.
2. **Merge to `main`** — Only `main` triggers production builds.
3. **CI detects changes** — If only JS/TS changed, an OTA update publishes to the `develop` channel. If native code changed, full builds start.
4. **Monitor Slack** — CI posts build status to Slack. Wait for all platforms (iOS + Android) to complete.
5. **Submit to stores** — Run `npm run submit:production` to push to App Store and Google Play.

---

## Common gotchas

- **Never commit `.env` files** — Use `.env.example` as the template. Real credentials go in `.env.development` (local) or environment variables (CI/production).

- **v2 still depends on v1** — Postgres tables reference Firestore IDs (`oldHid`, `oldUid`). Many v2 operations resolve the house in Firestore first. It's not a complete migration; it's a new layer on top of the old one.

- **Check-in/check-out inconsistency** — The code reads `default_check_in_<HomeType>` and `default_check_out_<HomeType>` from the `configurations` table, but also has a hardcoded fallback of 16:00 / 10:00. Confirm which values are active in production.

- **Editing rental/exchange notes** — When you edit a stay's notes in a rental or exchange booking, you must write to **both** the origin booking and its counterpart (the tenant's booking). If you only write to the origin, the next import cron will overwrite your changes because it reads from the counterpart.

- **Firestore vs Postgres split** — v1 endpoints read/write Firestore (bookings, calendar, slots). v2 endpoints read/write Postgres (keys, experiences). Don't mix them up or you'll get stale data.

- **Rate limiting on public endpoints** — `/api/public/events/ingest` allows 200 req/min (not the default 100). Check the endpoint's rate limit override before retrying.

- **Idempotency key reuse** — If you send the same `Idempotency-Key` with a different body, you get `idempotency_key_in_use` error. Either change the key or send the exact same body.

- **Empty string normalization** — Optional fields that arrive as empty strings or whitespace are normalized to absent before validation. The response includes `warnings[]` listing which fields were discarded. Required fields are not normalized.

- **Cursor pagination edge cases** — `?cursor=garbage` returns 400 `invalid_cursor`. `?limit=0` or negative returns 400 `validation_error`. `?limit=99999` silently truncates to the endpoint's max.

- **Sentry deduplication** — Errors can be reported multiple times (apiClient, React Query, error boundary). The code uses a WeakSet to track already-processed errors and avoid duplicates.

---

## Verification checklist

Before submitting work:

- [ ] **Environment variables** — All required `.env` variables are set locally. No real credentials in code or git.
- [ ] **API response shape** — If adding an endpoint, response matches conventions: `object` field, `request_id` in errors, proper HTTP status codes.
- [ ] **Error handling** — Errors use the standard envelope. `error.code` is stable (not `error.message`). `details[]` lists validation failures.
- [ ] **Pagination** — If returning a list, use cursor pagination with `has_more` and `next_cursor`.
- [ ] **Idempotency** — Mutations accept `Idempotency-Key` header and are safe for retries.
- [ ] **Rate limits** — Response includes `X-RateLimit-*` headers. Respects configured limits per endpoint.
- [ ] **Database consistency** — For bookings/rentals, changes are written to both origin and counterpart documents (if applicable).
- [ ] **Tests pass** — `npm run test` or `npm run lint` passes locally and in CI.
- [ ] **Deployment branch** — For production, changes are merged to `main` (mobile) or `develop` (backend).
- [ ] **Slack notification** — CI posts build/deploy status. Monitor for failures.
